title: Al-Humazah 104:1-3 with words spaced, and the questions
subject: Qur'an & Tajweed
source: Written for quran/y2 lesson 13 (Pupil PDF worksheet: Al-Humazah 104:1-3 with words spaced, and the questions)
intro: Lesson 13. Read each word slowly, pointing with your finger. Only the Arabic is the Qur'an; the English is a translation of its meaning.

arabic.text: وَيْلٌۭ لِّكُلِّ هُمَزَةٍۢ لُّمَزَةٍ (١) ٱلَّذِى جَمَعَ مَالًۭا وَعَدَّدَهُۥ (٢) يَحْسَبُ أَنَّ مَالَهُۥٓ أَخْلَدَهُۥ (٣)

head: Ayah
Translation of the meaning (Saheeh International)
rows: Woe to every scorner and mocker
Who collects wealth and [continuously] counts it.
He thinks that his wealth will make him immortal.

keywords.def: the one who mocks and backbites

questions.q: Chunk and link Al-Humazah 104:1-3 with the teacher.
Listening turns: today's group says 104:1-3 to the teacher, one by one. Everyone else: say it softly 3 times looking, 3 times without.
questions.a: Pupil recites with no help; the teacher marks hifdh and tajweed on the rubric and gives one target.

questions.q: Say one kind thing to someone at home today instead of teasing.

questions.a: A) Those who mock and backbite. 104:1: woe to every scorner and mocker.

questions.q: Al-Humazah 104:2: «ٱلَّذِى جَمَعَ ...» Which word comes next?
Think again: Is it ever funny to make fun of someone? How does it feel to be laughed at?
questions.a: It hurts. Allah warns those who mock and backbite (104:1); a Muslim's tongue is kind.
